SYNTHETIC LAB & DESIGN
Sovereign Federation Lab / Reader guide · edition 09

One person. Separate banking relationships.

Knowing who someone is does not tell every bank entity what it may see or change.

Implemented lab

The synthetic container lab is validated. Technical extension points on this page remain proposals unless explicitly identified as implemented. Understand the labels.

Start with the example · Look up a term

The same person can have different relationships

Aster is a synthetic person with a personal banking relationship and a role in a business account. Each relationship has its own identity, owner and policy. Updating shared contact information does not make every recipient entitled to that information.

ThingWhy it stays separate
Aster, the partyIdentifies the person. An eligible minimal party copy contains only id, global_party_id and party_type.
Personal relationshipDefines one business relationship and its permitted recipients and servicing data.
Business relationshipDefines another relationship. Permissions are not inherited from personal banking.
HoldingA product or account resource. A restriction can exclude this holding and its dependent rows.

A bank entity is not a database

The lab models 30 legal entities. Several can share a UK store while having different permissions. A recipient is selected by legal entity; its location is then resolved and checked separately. A nearby or shared database is never sufficient permission.

A copy does not become a second owner

An approved UK projection retains source ownership. It can show selected fields, but it does not become a UK-owned master or inherit authority to accept writes. Two UK entities can receive different projections in the same store without overwriting one another.

Technical detail: the current keys

ObjectIdentity
Partyowner_entity_id + party id; global_party_id links identity without merging rights.
Relationshipowner_entity_id + relationship id; several relationships for one party may coexist.
Recipient graphowner + scope + destination entity + business row id.
Placemententity_id → store_id + placement_version.
Separate teaching example: flat generated records

The generator also retains an older flat-record sandbox keyed by owner_entity_id + global_customer_id. It demonstrates movement and exclusions. This is not the normalized relationship key above; its record API should not be used as the operational model contract.

For implementers: engineering brief
HAND OFF TO ENGINEERING

Build this component

A focused prompt with scope, contracts and acceptance criteria.

Read the full prompt
Preserve the normalized business model and independent party/relationship scopes. Keep owner-qualified party and relationship UUIDs, shared identity without unioned rights, and recipient keys qualified by owner, scope, destination and business row. The retained flat owner/global_customer_id fixture is a separate demonstration. Test several relationships for one party, independent owners, eligible minimal party identity, recipient-specific fields and source-side exclusions in real CockroachDB/OPA. Do not add identity matching or merge/split governance without a separate approved scope.
